_meta.name: proverbs_multilingual
_meta.note: traditional proverbs/idioms across languages; originals are folk material (public domain); English glosses are this repo's own translations; humor_hook explains the reusable comic engine

text: Camarón que se duerme, se lo lleva la corriente. — The shrimp that falls asleep is swept away by the current.

meta.gloss: Doze off and the current takes you.
meta.humor_hook: tiny animal as the professional-consequences everyman

text: El que madruga, Dios lo ayuda... pero el que se acuesta tarde ve cosas. — God helps the early riser... but the night owl sees things.

meta.gloss: Early birds get help; night owls get stories.
meta.humor_hook: pious setup, mischievous tag — rule-of-three deviation built in

text: Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué. — Don't sell the bear's skin before killing the bear.

meta.gloss: Don't sell the bearskin first.
meta.humor_hook: premature-victory frame; swap the bear for any modern deliverable

text: Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid. — Little by little, the bird builds its nest.

meta.gloss: Small steps finish the nest.
meta.humor_hook: patience canon; ironic against sprint-deadline culture

text: Das Leben ist kein Ponyhof. — Life is not a pony farm.

meta.gloss: Life is no pony farm.
meta.humor_hook: grim wisdom delivered through an aggressively cute image

text: Wer zwei Hasen jagt, fängt keinen. — Who chases two rabbits catches none.

meta.gloss: Chase two rabbits, catch zero.
meta.humor_hook: multitasking fallacy as small-game hunting

text: Der Teufel steckt im Detail. — The devil is in the detail.

meta.gloss: The devil hides in the details.
meta.humor_hook: cosmic evil scaled down to paperwork

text: Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare. — Between saying and doing lies the sea.

meta.gloss: An ocean sits between saying and doing.
meta.humor_hook: roadmap-vs-reality gap as geography

text: Chi dorme non piglia pesci. — Who sleeps catches no fish.

meta.gloss: Sleepers catch no fish.
meta.humor_hook: hustle canon; inverts cleanly for rest-advocacy irony

text: Festina lente. — Hurry slowly.

meta.gloss: Make haste slowly.
meta.humor_hook: two-word oxymoron; the shortest script opposition on record

text: Errare humanum est, perseverare diabolicum. — To err is human; to persist in error is diabolical.

meta.gloss: Erring is human; repeating the error is devilish.
meta.humor_hook: escalation frame: the second bug is a moral failing

text: Der mentsh trakht un got lakht. — Man plans and God laughs.

meta.gloss: Man plans, God laughs.
meta.humor_hook: the canonical planning-futility frame; every roadmap joke rents this cache

text: A halber emes iz a gantser lign. — Half a truth is a whole lie.

meta.gloss: A half-truth is a full lie.
meta.humor_hook: arithmetic of honesty; audit-season material

text: 骑虎难下 (qí hǔ nán xià) — When riding a tiger, it is hard to dismount.

meta.gloss: Hard to get off the tiger you are riding.
meta.humor_hook: sunk-cost frame with apex-predator stakes; fits any legacy migration

text: 拔苗助长 (bá miáo zhù zhǎng) — Pulling up seedlings to help them grow.

meta.gloss: Yanking sprouts to speed the harvest.
meta.humor_hook: helpful sabotage; micromanagement in agricultural form

text: 猿も木から落ちる (saru mo ki kara ochiru) — Even monkeys fall from trees.

meta.gloss: Even monkeys fall out of trees.
meta.humor_hook: expert-failure frame; the senior engineer's outage

text: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず (nito wo ou mono wa itto wo mo ezu) — He who chases two hares catches neither.

meta.gloss: Chase two hares, catch neither.
meta.humor_hook: same two-rabbit engine as the German — a cross-lingual frame match on purpose

text: Доверяй, но проверяй (doveryai, no proveryai) — Trust, but verify.

meta.gloss: Trust, but verify.
meta.humor_hook: wholesome-paranoia frame; code-review canon

text: Работа не волк — в лес не убежит (rabota ne volk) — Work is not a wolf; it won't run off into the forest.

meta.gloss: Work is no wolf; it will not flee to the woods.
meta.humor_hook: procrastination defended with wildlife biology

text: القرد في عين أمه غزال (al-qird fi 'ayn ummihi ghazal) — In its mother's eye, the monkey is a gazelle.

meta.gloss: To its mother, the monkey is a gazelle.
meta.humor_hook: founder-demo frame: love recategorizes the product

text: الجمل لا يرى اعوجاج رقبته (al-jamal la yara i'wijaj raqbatih) — The camel cannot see the crookedness of its own neck.

meta.gloss: The camel never sees its own crooked neck.
meta.humor_hook: code-reviewer blind-spot frame with a camel

text: नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा (naach na jaane aangan tedha) — Doesn't know how to dance, says the courtyard is crooked.

meta.gloss: Can't dance, blames the crooked courtyard.
meta.humor_hook: the it-works-on-my-machine frame, several centuries early

text: ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा (oont ke munh mein jeera) — A cumin seed in a camel's mouth.

meta.gloss: A cumin seed for a camel.
meta.humor_hook: comic disproportion frame; the 2% raise, the 5-minute standup slot

text: Damlaya damlaya göl olur. — Drop by drop, a lake is formed.

meta.gloss: Drip by drip it becomes a lake.
meta.humor_hook: compounding frame; also the tech-debt origin story

text: Quem não tem cão, caça com gato. — Who has no dog hunts with a cat.

meta.gloss: No dog? Hunt with the cat.
meta.humor_hook: duct-tape-engineering frame with an uncooperative animal

text: Nie mój cyrk, nie moje małpy. — Not my circus, not my monkeys.

meta.gloss: Not my circus, not my monkeys.
meta.humor_hook: boundary-setting frame; org-chart chaos disclaimed in two clauses

text: Nu komt de aap uit de mouw. — Now the monkey comes out of the sleeve.

meta.gloss: The monkey finally comes out of the sleeve.
meta.humor_hook: hidden-motive reveal frame with built-in slapstick imagery

text: Även små grytor har öron. — Even small pots have ears.

meta.gloss: Even little pots have ears.
meta.humor_hook: eavesdropping frame; the muted-mic betrayal

text: Is minic a bhris béal duine a shrón. — Many a time a man's mouth broke his nose.

meta.gloss: A mouth often breaks its own nose.
meta.humor_hook: self-inflicted-consequences frame; reply-all in proverb form

text: Όποιος βιάζεται σκοντάφτει (opoios viazetai skontaftei) — Whoever hurries, stumbles.

meta.gloss: The hurried one trips.
meta.humor_hook: haste-failure frame; hotfix canon

text: 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다 (wonsungido namueseo tteoreojinda) — Even monkeys fall from trees.

meta.gloss: Even monkeys fall from trees.
meta.humor_hook: third language sharing the expert-failure frame — canon travels

text: Haraka haraka haina baraka. — Hurry hurry has no blessing.

meta.gloss: Rush-rush carries no blessing.
meta.humor_hook: rhymed haste-failure frame; deploy-Friday liturgy

text: אין הנחתום מעיד על עיסתו (ein hanachtom me'id al isato) — The baker may not testify about his own dough.

meta.gloss: No baker vouches for his own dough.
meta.humor_hook: self-review conflict-of-interest frame; the PR that approves itself

text: موش تو سوراخ نمی‌رفت جارو به دمش می‌بست (mush tu surakh nemiraft) — The mouse couldn't fit through the hole, so it tied a broom to its tail.

meta.gloss: Couldn't fit the hole; added a broom to its tail.
meta.humor_hook: scope-creep frame in rodent logistics

text: Det er ingen skam å snu. — There is no shame in turning back.

meta.gloss: No shame in turning around.
meta.humor_hook: mountain-safety canon; the rollback absolution

text: Ei kukaan ole seppä syntyessään. — No one is born a blacksmith.

meta.gloss: Nobody is born a smith.
meta.humor_hook: beginner-grace frame; junior-dev absolution with anvils

text: Man plans and God laughs.

meta.gloss: Man plans and God laughs.
meta.humor_hook: English rendering of the Yiddish classic — deliberate cross-lingual surface pair for the precedent demo
